extra.message: In Student.create the user-supplied `name` is interpolated into the SQL string via Python `%` string formatting ("VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name}) and the resulting string is passed to cur.execute() with NO parameterization. `name` originates from POST data['name'] in views.students (views.py:57). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. a name of `'); UPDATE users SET is_admin=true;--` to escalate privileges or exfiltrate data.

Jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False. All template variables rendered via {{ ... }} are therefore output without HTML escaping, enabling Cross-Site Scripting. User-controlled values rendered unescaped include review text (course.jinja2:22), student names (students.jinja2:16), and course title/description (courses.jinja2:17-18, course.jinja2:14-15).

Stored XSS: review.review_text is rendered with {{ review.review_text }} without escaping (autoescape is disabled in app.py:35). The review text is user-controlled, submitted via POST to /courses/{id}/review (views.py:121,129) and stored in the database, then displayed to any user viewing the course. An attacker can inject <script> to execute in victims' browsers.

Stored XSS: the student `name` is rendered with {{ name }} without escaping (autoescape disabled in app.py:35). The name is user-controlled, submitted via POST to /students/ (views.py:57) and listed on the students page, allowing script injection that executes for anyone viewing the students list.

Stored XSS: course.title (and course.description on line 18) are rendered with {{ ... }} without escaping (autoescape disabled in app.py:35). Both fields are user-controlled, submitted via POST to /courses/ (views.py:89-90) and rendered on the courses listing, enabling script injection.

The evaluate() handler (POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id}) creates marks/grades but has no @authorize() decorator and performs no authentication or authorization check. The template (course.jinja2:41) only renders the evaluate form for auth_user.is_admin, indicating this action is intended to be admin-only. Any unauthenticated user can POST to set arbitrary grades, a broken access control / missing authorization vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The courses() handler accepts POST to create a new course but has no @authorize() decorator and no auth check. The template (courses.jinja2:25) only renders the create form when auth_user and auth_user.is_admin, indicating this is intended to be an admin-only action. Any unauthenticated user can create courses, a broken access control vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The students() handler accepts POST to create a new student but has no @authorize() decorator and no authentication check. The template (students.jinja2:21) only renders the create form for authenticated auth_user, indicating creation should require login. Any unauthenticated user can create students (and exploit the SQL injection in Student.create).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The review() handler accepts POST to create a course review but has no @authorize() decorator and no authentication check, allowing any unauthenticated user to submit reviews. Combined with the disabled CSRF middleware and XSS in review rendering, this enables unauthenticated spam/injection of malicious reviews.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The CSRF middleware (csrf_middleware defined in middlewares.py:26) is commented out in the application middleware list. All state-changing POST endpoints (login, logout, create student/course/review, evaluate) are therefore vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery. An attacker can craft a malicious page that forces an authenticated victim's browser to perform actions such as creating records, setting grades, or logging the user out.

check_password() verifies credentials by comparing the stored hash to md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(). MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing: it is fast (easy to brute-force/GPU-crack) and uses no salt, so identical passwords yield identical hashes. If the database is leaked (e.g. via the SQL injection in Student.create), all user passwords can be recovered trivially. A slow salted KDF (bcrypt/argon2) should be used instead.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The session storage is created with RedisStorage(app['redis'], httponly=False), so the session cookie is set without the HttpOnly flag (and the app is served over plain HTTP on port 8080 with no Secure flag). The session cookie becomes readable from JavaScript, which combined with the XSS vulnerabilities allows an attacker to steal session tokens and hijack accounts.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The aiohttp Application is instantiated with debug=True. In debug mode aiohttp exposes detailed error pages/tracebacks (e.g. when views access missing form fields like data['username']/data['name'] and raise KeyError), leaking internal paths, source code snippets, and stack traces to attackers (CWE-209). Debug mode should never be enabled in a deployed application.

The database credentials are hardcoded in config/dev.yaml as user 'postgres' with password 'postgres' (the well-known PostgreSQL default). These credentials are loaded by services/db.py:15-19 to build the connection DSN. Hardcoded default DB credentials allow an attacker who reaches the database service to authenticate trivially.

The seed fixtures create application accounts with hardcoded, trivially guessable passwords, including an administrator: 'superadmin'/'superadmin' (is_admin=TRUE), 'j.doe'/'password', 's.king'/'password', and 'p.parker'/'spidey' (passwords stored as md5). These default credentials allow an attacker to log in directly, and the admin account grants full administrative access.
